plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on feedback directives: replace uniform thickness initialization with deterministic quarter-wave estimates at passband center wavelengths (3.30 μm for CH4, 4.25 μm for CO2), and cap maximum layer thickness at 950 nm to prevent optimizer saturation. Four complementary routes explore: (1) 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 with quarter-wave initialization at methane band, (2) 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 with quarter-wave initialization at CO2 band, (3) 20-layer Ge/Nb2O5 alternative material pair with quarter-wave initialization, (4) 24-layer maximum-count ZnS/MgF2 to test layer-count benefit. All routes maintain parent_route_id='route_01' per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 with Quarter-Wave Initialization at Methane Band Center
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses to quarter-wave optical thickness at the methane passband center (3.30 μm) rather than uniform random values will provide a physically meaningful starting point that accelerates convergence toward high transmittance in both passbands while maintaining stopband suppression.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack principle: alternating high/low index layers with optical thickness λ/4 at design wavelength creates constructive interference for reflection at that wavelength. For dual-band transmission, thicknesses must be optimized away from pure quarter-wave to create transmission windows at both target bands.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | CaF2 substrate (22 finite layers total, alternating sequence starting with ZnS)

Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds [50, 950] nm prevent optimizer saturation
ZnS and MgF2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for alternating index multilayers
Transfer matrix method for coherent thin-film interference

Bounded thickness prevents optimizer from hitting upper boundary prematurely
22 layers provide sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization
known_risks: Quarter-wave at one band may not generalize well to second passband
May require more optimization iterations to escape local minimum
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate with alternating ZnS (high index) and MgF2 (low index) layers under normal unpolarized illumination. Initialize all 22 layer thicknesses to quarter-wave optical thickness at 3300 nm center wavelength (ZnS: n*thickness = 3300/4 nm, MgF2: n*thickness = 3300/4 nm using material refractive indices). Constrain all thicknesses to [50, 950] nm bounds. Use gradient-based thickness optimization to maximize mean transmittance in passbands (3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm) while minimizing mean transmittance in stopbands (2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm). Evaluate using coherent transfer matrix method across 2500-5000 nm wavelength range. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Replaced uniform random thickness initialization with deterministic quarter-wave estimates at methane band center (3300 nm) per feedback directive; capped maximum thickness at 950 nm to prevent optimizer saturation at 1100 nm boundary

routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack principle applied at longer wavelength (4.25 μm) creates different initial optical path distribution, potentially favoring the second passband while still allowing optimization to recover first passband transmission.

routes.title: 20-Layer Ge/Nb2O5 Alternative Material Pair with Quarter-Wave Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Ge/Nb2O5 material pair (referenced in evidence for methane sensor bandpass filters) will provide higher index contrast than ZnS/MgF2, enabling steeper spectral slopes and better stopband suppression with fewer layers (20 instead of 22).
routes.design_principle: Higher refractive index contrast between alternating layers produces stronger interference effects per layer pair, potentially achieving equivalent performance with reduced layer count. Evidence shows Ge/Nb2O5 successfully deposited for 3300 nm methane sensor bandpass filters.

routes.title: 24-Layer Maximum-Count ZnS/MgF2 with Quarter-Wave Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Using the maximum allowed layer count (24 layers) will provide additional degrees of freedom for the optimizer to simultaneously satisfy both passband transmission and stopband suppression requirements, potentially achieving higher best_target_score than 22-layer configurations.
routes.design_principle: More layers provide more optimization variables and enable more complex interference patterns. Evidence indicates more layers produce steeper spectral slopes and higher out-of-band blocking, though transmission may drop and passbands acquire spectral ripple as thickness increases.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:139773493:s2chunk:139773493:23617:24948:3169b780e7b9ea48 and s2-chunk:CorpusId:139773493:s2chunk:139773493:25021:26346:5f1917d4b80dcb33 demonstrated Ge/Nb2O5 multilayer bandpass filters successfully deposited for methane sensor at 3300 nm, motivating route_01_ref_ge_nb2o5 as alternative material pair.

Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:227248144:s2chunk:227248144:13756:16101:11bc1b8f56987299 established that more layers produce steeper spectral slopes and higher out-of-band blocking, motivating route_01_ref_24layer_max to test maximum layer count.

Feedback directives explicitly required replacing uniform random initialization with quarter-wave estimates at passband center wavelengths and capping thickness at 950 nm, which all four routes implement.

Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:17683472:s2chunk:17683472:29776:32010:c36d261f52b76fe1 warned that thicker coatings increase vacuum chamber residence time and make transmissive behavior harder to control, noted in route_01_ref_24layer_max known_risks.
unresolved_decisions: Whether quarter-wave initialization wavelength (3300 nm vs 4250 nm) significantly affects final optimized performance
Whether Ge/Nb2O5 material pair provides sufficient advantage over ZnS/MgF2 to justify potential absorption losses
Whether 24 layers provide meaningful improvement over 22 layers or exhibit diminishing returns
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
